transcript: in honor of the Wicked movie coming out this week I think it's finally time to reveal my deepest, darkest secret so if you follow my content you know that I famously rarely see shows more than once but in another life many years ago I was something of a Wicked super fan and in fact by an extremely wide margin Wicked is the show that I've seen the most in my life I will tell you how many times I've seen it but first I have to give context: The story goes that I was a very young person growing up in my hometown of San Franciscoc California where Wicked was playing an extended sit-down production for almost two years they had a lottery back when lotteries were in-person and still super cheap I think it was like $20 or something and my parents I think were giving me some sort of an allowance and I literally spent all of it on Wicked lottery tickets a big part of it was actually just a social experience for me there were a lot of other superfans who I got to become friendly with. We would try to see all of the understudies the standbys, the replacements Of course all of the milestone performances of course you know I was a regular at the stage door some of the actors in the production were Eden Espinosa she replaced Teal Wicks as Elphaba Deedee Magno Hall was Nessa Rose I believe she's mostly known for her voice work in Steven Universe nowadays Etai Benson who would later go on to star in the Band's Visit and the Company revival also fun fact that Alyssa Fox who's now a very well established long time Elphaba actually started out as a 2nd cover in the San Francisco production and I saw her first and second ever performances as Elphaba my real claim to fame is that the standby Felicia Ricci actually wrote a memoir about her time in Wicked and I am actually mentioned in this book by name on page 201 not that I'm biased but it's actually a really entertaining read I do highly recommend it! A lot of people very understandably assumed that Wicked was like my favourite show of all time and that I was completely obsessed with it and even at that time that wasn't entirely true obviously I loved it I wouldn't have seen it so many times if I didn't love it but I think after seeing it so many times I kinda became numb to the story and it was really just more about escaping into this world plus as I said it was a social experience and a parasocial experience I was also viewing it very technically like spotting the differences between the performances and also just learning a lot about how big productions like Wicked operate sort of a situation of like it happened to be Wicked but it didn't necessarily have to be maybe that's partly why despite my deep history with the show I haven't really felt moved to talk about the Wicked movie at all although the other reason is that I kinda feel like we've been burned a lot by movie musicals in the last few years and so I've kind of just been assuming this whole time that the Wicked movie is gonna be bad I'm now hearing that's not the case which is nice but we'll see and now as promised I will reveal how many times I've seen the show working backward a little bit I saw it 4 times AFTER the San Francisco production most recently in 2021 I went to the reopening performance on Broadway and at that point it had been nine years since I had last seen it and during the two years or so that it was playing in San Francisco I saw Wicked 34 times bringing me up to a lifetime total of 38 the single production that I've seen second-most after Wicked I saw five times so like I said it's a pretty wide margin
